key_insight: MetaboNet consolidates multiple public Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) datasets into the largest standardized, ready-to-use public resource for T1D management research, enabling consistent benchmarking and faster algorithm development.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation and heterogeneity across public T1D datasets that make integration, preprocessing, and fair comparison of algorithms time-consuming and error-prone.
method: Aggregate multiple publicly available T1D datasets and harmonize schema, units, timestamps, and variable names into a unified format.
Apply de-identification, quality-control filters, and standardized metadata/annotations to ensure usability and reproducibility.
Provide documentation, example preprocessing code, and benchmark tasks to make the dataset immediately accessible for ML workflows.
impact: Offers AI/ML practitioners a single, curated dataset that reduces preprocessing overhead, improves reproducibility, and enables fairer comparison and generalization testing of glucose prediction and insulin-delivery models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing dataset sources → harmonization (units/timezones) → QC/de‑identification → standardized output
Before/after comparison table or bar chart showing heterogeneity removed (e.g., differing units, missing fields) and increased sample size
Heatmap or timeline of aggregated patient CGM/insulin data density to show coverage and temporal depth
Icon set: CGM trace, insulin pump/syringe, data/documentation, benchmark chart
paper_title: MetaboNet: The Largest Publicly Available Consolidated Dataset for Type 1 Diabetes Management
paper_authors: Miriam K. Wolff, Peter Calhoun, Eleonora Maria Aiello, Yao Qin, Sam F. Royston
